result.title: Dual-Manifold Variational Autoencoders
result.summary: In latent diffusion models, expanding the latent dimension of variational autoencoders (VAEs) is essential to push the upper bound of reconstruction quality. However, without explicit structural constraints, such unregularized expansion easily yields a rugged and ill-conditioned latent manifold, causing generated latents to drift off the manifold during generation (i.e., off-manifold problem). Recent works smooth this manifold by using external foundation models (e.g., DINOv2) as a topological regularizer. However, we argue that tying the latent space to frozen external priors inherently restricts generalization: bound by their pre-training distributions and semantic biases, they may fail to capture faithful visual details on out-of-distribution domains. Observing that low-dimensional latents naturally form a smoother, generation-friendly manifold, we propose dual-manifold VAE (DM-VAE) to leverage internal representations as a topological regularizer. Specifically, DM-VAE pairs a high-dimensional reconstructive branch with a low-dimensional branch that extracts a clean topological skeleton, anchoring the high-dimensional manifold to this smooth subspace. Building upon this framework, we further introduce topological representation alignment (TRA) to supervise intermediate generator features during training, and internal guidance with topological skeleton (IG_TS) to guide structural components while preserving high-frequency details at inference. On ImageNet-1K (256x256), our foundation-model-free DM-VAE achieves a state-of-the-art rFID of 0.12 and a generation FID50K of 1.28 (w/o CFG) and 1.20 (w/CFG), and further reaches 1.11 when orthogonally combined with DINOv2.

AI.brief_summary: 提出双流形 VAE（DM-VAE）：用低维分支提取干净的拓扑骨架，将高维重建潜空间锚定到该光滑子空间，替代对 DINOv2 等外部基础模型的依赖，并配合训练期的拓扑表示对齐与推理期的内部骨架引导，在 ImageNet-1K 上取得很低的 rFID 与 FID。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「高维潜空间易产生崎岖流形并在生成中漂移」的观察，以及用低维内部骨架做正则、推理期施加内部引导的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的几何稳定性与漂移控制提供可核查线索；但研究对象是图像生成而非视觉推理，需较多核查。
